troubleshoot-no-dial-tone-on-a-desk-phon.title: Troubleshoot no dial tone on a desk phone
prechecks: Check handset/cabling, device power/PoE and whether the phone is registered to the expected voice/Teams service.
Check Microsoft 365/Teams Phone or the organisation's PBX/voice service health before changing the physical phone.
Check the assigned device profile, line/extension/account state and network reachability before reset or firmware action.
troubleshoot-no-dial-tone-on-a-desk-phon.rollback: Record the current approved phone profile and firmware/update state. Revert only where the vendor/platform supports an approved rollback; otherwise restore the previous profile/configuration or use the supported recovery process.
troubleshoot-no-dial-tone-on-a-desk-phon.symptom_match: "Voice/Telephony is degraded", "Teams Phone is not working".
troubleshoot-no-dial-tone-on-a-desk-phon.duplication: Related to Batch B-2 #1 (Teams Phone Device). Merge with that procedure; this is a child branch for the "no dial tone" symptom.

troubleshoot-offline-files-synchronisati.title: Troubleshoot Offline Files synchronisation
prechecks: Confirm network/VPN reachability to the authoritative file server/share and verify the server copy is accessible.
Check Windows Offline Files/Sync Center state, cache capacity and exact conflict/error rather than deleting the CSC cache.
Identify file locks/conflicts and establish which copy is authoritative before reconciling data.
troubleshoot-offline-files-synchronisati.rollback: Preserve unsynchronised local data before reset. If an authorised GPO/configuration change caused the issue, restore the previous policy. Resolve conflicts from a verified authoritative copy or backup; do not overwrite local/server data blindly.
troubleshoot-offline-files-synchronisati.symptom_match: "Network drive is not accessible", "File sync is failing".

troubleshoot-one-way-audio.title: Troubleshoot one-way audio
prechecks: Step 0: check the applicable voice/UC provider service health before changing firewall, client or endpoint configuration.
Capture call/session ID, direction of failed media and affected parties, then verify RTP/SRTP/STUN/TURN/media path as appropriate to the platform.
Confirm local microphone/speaker/device selection works outside the call so endpoint hardware is not confused with network/media failure.
troubleshoot-one-way-audio.rollback: Capture the relevant firewall/NAT/media policy before change. If an authorised policy change causes regression, restore the previous approved policy immediately and re-test two-way media.
troubleshoot-one-way-audio.symptom_match: "Audio or microphone is not working", "Voice/Telephony is degraded".
troubleshoot-one-way-audio.duplication: Related to #4 (macOS audio) and #10 (Citrix audio) – this is the generic parent.

troubleshoot-onedrive-synchronisation.title: Troubleshoot OneDrive synchronisation
prechecks: Step 0: check Microsoft 365/OneDrive service health before local-client remediation.
Verify OneDrive web access, storage quota, client sync status and the exact blocked/conflicted items.
Establish the local/cloud source of truth and preserve unsynchronised local data before unlinking, resetting or moving files.
troubleshoot-onedrive-synchronisation.rollback: Use OneDrive version history/recycle bin or preserved local data to recover a confirmed bad sync result. If a managed OneDrive/KFM policy change caused the issue, restore the previous approved policy; do not overwrite cloud data to force synchronisation.
troubleshoot-onedrive-synchronisation.symptom_match: "Microsoft 365 feature is not working", "OneDrive sync is failing".
troubleshoot-onedrive-synchronisation.duplication: Related to Batch B-5 #20 (Google Drive sync) – keep distinct for platform-specific steps.

troubleshoot-pop-ups-required-by-a-busin.title: Troubleshoot pop-ups required by a business application
prechecks: Confirm the business application's approved URL/domain and whether the block comes from browser settings, an extension or managed browser/GPO policy.
Allow pop-ups only for the minimum approved site scope required by the application.
Use private/incognito testing only to isolate extensions/session state; do not bypass a corporate security policy without approval.
troubleshoot-pop-ups-required-by-a-busin.rollback: Remove the site exception or restore the previous approved browser policy if the change causes unwanted pop-ups or weakens security.
troubleshoot-pop-ups-required-by-a-busin.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

troubleshoot-powerpoint-presentation-dis.title: Troubleshoot PowerPoint presentation display
prechecks: Confirm the external display/projector is detected and works outside PowerPoint.
Check Duplicate/Extend mode, Presenter View, slide-show monitor selection and supported resolution/scaling.
Test the presentation on the primary display or another approved output path to isolate PowerPoint from OS/display hardware.
troubleshoot-powerpoint-presentation-dis.rollback: Record display/PowerPoint settings before change. Restore the previous approved display/graphics configuration if a confirmed change caused regression; use supported driver rollback only where available.
troubleshoot-powerpoint-presentation-dis.symptom_match: "Display is not working", "Application is not working".
troubleshoot-powerpoint-presentation-dis.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

troubleshoot-printing-from-macos.title: Troubleshoot printing from macOS
prechecks: Confirm the printer is reachable/available and can be used by another authorised client before treating the issue as macOS-specific.
Check the macOS printer queue, selected driver/PPD or AirPrint path and test from another application.
Check print-server/printer logs and network/DNS reachability when the queue is network-based.
troubleshoot-printing-from-macos.rollback: Record the current queue/driver configuration. Restore the previous approved printer/driver configuration if a confirmed change caused regression; use vendor-supported packages rather than arbitrary driver downgrades.
troubleshoot-printing-from-macos.symptom_match: "Printing or scanning is not working", "Apple macOS device is not working correctly".
troubleshoot-printing-from-macos.duplication: Unique. Related to "application printing" (#3 B-5) but macOS-specific.

troubleshoot-remote-desktop-connection-f.title: Troubleshoot Remote Desktop connection failure
prechecks: Determine whether the target is a server or workstation and confirm the approved management path and business impact.
Test DNS/network reachability and TCP 3389 (or the organisation's configured RDP path); ICMP success is not required.

Check Remote Desktop service/configuration, firewall policy and user/group entitlement. For servers/VMs, ensure an approved console or out-of-band management path is available before remote policy changes.
troubleshoot-remote-desktop-connection-f.rollback: Capture firewall/GPO/RDP configuration before change. If an authorised change causes lockout, restore the previous configuration through the approved console/out-of-band/hypervisor management path; do not describe that path as a security bypass.
troubleshoot-remote-desktop-connection-f.symptom_match: "Cannot sign in", "Windows device is not working correctly".

troubleshoot-scan-to-email.title: Troubleshoot scan to email
prechecks: Confirm the MFP has network/DNS reachability to the approved SMTP relay or mail service.
Check SMTP relay/connector authentication, TLS/certificate requirements and exact delivery error/log.
Check message/attachment size and recipient/mail-flow restrictions relevant to the failed scan.
troubleshoot-scan-to-email.rollback: Export or record the MFP SMTP/relay settings before change. Restore the previous approved SMTP configuration if an authorised change causes regression.
troubleshoot-scan-to-email.symptom_match: "Scanning is not working", "Email is not being delivered".

troubleshoot-secure-or-follow-me-printin.title: Troubleshoot secure or follow-me printing
prechecks: Check the print-management platform/release service health and whether the user's held job exists.
Verify badge/PIN/identity mapping and release-station/printer connectivity.
Check print-server queue, management-agent/client and recent policy/software changes before deleting jobs.
troubleshoot-secure-or-follow-me-printin.rollback: Capture print-management policy/version and queue configuration before change. Restore the previous approved policy/software/configuration if a confirmed update causes regression; preserve required job evidence.
troubleshoot-secure-or-follow-me-printin.duplication: Related to "print server outage" but specific to secure printing. Keep distinct.

troubleshoot-server-high-cpu.title: Troubleshoot server high CPU
prechecks: This compatibility page is a duplicate of the canonical high-CPU runbook and must route to it.
Preserve the historical server-specific URL while the canonical procedure gains an explicit server/service scope branch.
troubleshoot-server-high-cpu.rollback: No independent remediation is permitted after deprecation; rollback and verification belong to the canonical high-CPU utilisation procedure.
troubleshoot-server-high-cpu.duplication: **CRITICAL DUPLICATE.** This is **exactly** the same as Batch B-5 #22. Merge immediately.

troubleshoot-server-high-memory.title: Troubleshoot server high memory
prechecks: This compatibility page is a duplicate of the canonical high-memory runbook and must route to it.
Preserve the historical server-specific URL while the canonical procedure gains an explicit server/service scope branch.
troubleshoot-server-high-memory.rollback: No independent remediation is permitted after deprecation; rollback and verification belong to the canonical high-memory utilisation procedure.
troubleshoot-server-high-memory.duplication: **CRITICAL DUPLICATE.** This is **exactly** the same as Batch B-5 #24. Merge immediately.

troubleshoot-sharepoint-access.title: Troubleshoot SharePoint access
prechecks: Check Microsoft 365/SharePoint service health and whether the issue affects one user, one site/library or multiple users.
Verify site/group/permission state and whether the site is locked/read-only or access is restricted by Conditional Access/sharing policy.
Test SharePoint web access from a clean browser session before changing permissions.
troubleshoot-sharepoint-access.rollback: Capture existing permissions/site policy before change. Restore the previous approved permission/policy if an authorised change broadens or removes access incorrectly.
troubleshoot-sharepoint-access.symptom_match: "Access is denied or missing", "SharePoint is not accessible".
troubleshoot-sharepoint-access.duplication: Unique. Related to Batch B-5 #14 (Directory sync) but specific to SharePoint.

troubleshoot-sharepoint-document-synchro.title: Troubleshoot SharePoint document synchronisation
prechecks: This compatibility page is being consolidated into the OneDrive synchronisation runbook because SharePoint library sync uses the OneDrive sync client.
Preserve the historical SharePoint-specific URL while the canonical OneDrive procedure gains a SharePoint-library branch.
troubleshoot-sharepoint-document-synchro.rollback: No independent sync reset is permitted after deprecation; source-of-truth, rollback and verification belong to the canonical OneDrive synchronisation procedure.
troubleshoot-sharepoint-document-synchro.symptom_match: "OneDrive sync is failing", "SharePoint is not accessible".
troubleshoot-sharepoint-document-synchro.duplication: **Duplicate of #4 (OneDrive synchronisation).** They are the same underlying sync engine. Merge these two.

troubleshoot-sharepoint-external-sharing.title: Troubleshoot SharePoint external sharing
prechecks: Step 0: verify the external-sharing request, data owner/sponsor and required approval before creating or expanding external access.
Check tenant/site external-sharing policy, sensitivity/retention controls and the intended recipient identity/domain.
Check existing link type, expiration, access scope and whether a more restrictive sharing method can satisfy the business need.
troubleshoot-sharepoint-external-sharing.rollback: If a share/link was created incorrectly, revoke the specific link/access immediately through the approved SharePoint administration path, preserve the audit trail and assess whether exposure occurred.
troubleshoot-sharepoint-external-sharing.symptom_match: "A security or compliance concern is reported", "Access is denied or missing".

troubleshoot-single-sign-on-failure.title: Troubleshoot single sign-on failure
prechecks: Step 0: check Microsoft Entra/identity-provider and application/service-provider health before changing SSO configuration.
Review sign-in/federation logs for the exact SAML/OIDC/OAuth error, request/correlation ID and affected scope.
Check federation metadata, redirect/ACS URI, issuer/entity ID, certificate/secret expiry and clock/time validity as appropriate.
troubleshoot-single-sign-on-failure.rollback: Export/capture the working SSO/federation configuration before change. If an authorised metadata/certificate/secret configuration change causes failure, restore the previous approved configuration through the identity/application administration path.
troubleshoot-single-sign-on-failure.duplication: Related to Batch B-4 #9 (SAML error) – this is the broader SSO parent.

troubleshoot-ssh-access.title: Troubleshoot SSH access
prechecks: Test DNS/network reachability and TCP 22 (or the configured SSH port); ICMP success is not required.
Check sshd/service state and authentication logs using an approved local, hypervisor or out-of-band console when remote SSH is unavailable.
Verify the account/key, home/.ssh ownership and permissions, and relevant PAM/SSSD/identity-provider state before editing sshd_config.
troubleshoot-ssh-access.rollback: Back up SSH/authentication configuration before change and maintain an approved console/out-of-band recovery path. Validate configuration syntax before reload/restart; restore the previous approved configuration if access worsens.
troubleshoot-ssh-access.symptom_match: "Cannot sign in", "Linux device is not working correctly".
troubleshoot-ssh-access.duplication: Related to Batch B-5 #27 (Linux sign-in) – this is the SSH-specific branch of that.

troubleshoot-usb-storage-not-detected.title: Troubleshoot USB storage not detected
prechecks: Check Device Manager/Disk Management and test the device/port on a known-good authorised system where policy permits.
Check endpoint security, DLP and Group Policy/MDM for intentional USB-storage restrictions before treating the block as a fault.
Check for hardware/media failure and stop if the device may contain required evidence or damaged business data.
troubleshoot-usb-storage-not-detected.rollback: Do not revert a security policy merely to enable USB storage. If an authorised policy change caused unintended blocking, restore the previous approved policy. Restore driver/configuration only through supported endpoint-management controls.
troubleshoot-usb-storage-not-detected.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

troubleshoot-vdi-multi-monitor-support.title: Troubleshoot VDI multi-monitor support
prechecks: Confirm the physical monitors work locally using the canonical external-monitor procedure before treating this as VDI-specific.
Check Citrix/VMware/AVD client multi-monitor capability, client version and relevant session/policy limits.
Compare single-monitor and multi-monitor sessions and check resolution/scaling/GPU/display policy constraints.
troubleshoot-vdi-multi-monitor-support.rollback: Record client and VDI display policy before change. Restore the previous approved client/policy if an authorised update causes regression; keep the generic physical-monitor remediation separate.
troubleshoot-vdi-multi-monitor-support.symptom_match: "Display is not working", "VDI session is not working".
troubleshoot-vdi-multi-monitor-support.duplication: **Related to Batch B-4 #27-29 & B-5 #30 (External Monitors).** This is the VDI-specific branch. Keep distinct but cross-reference to the generic external monitor parent.

troubleshoot-vdi-performance.title: Troubleshoot VDI performance
prechecks: Determine whether performance affects one session, one host, one pool/site or all users.
Check host CPU, memory, storage I/O, session density and broker/VDA/agent health.
Check client-to-gateway/host latency, packet loss and bandwidth plus recent image/policy/host changes.
troubleshoot-vdi-performance.rollback: Capture host/image/policy state before change. If a confirmed patch/image/configuration change causes degradation, restore the previous approved image/policy or drain/migrate sessions to a known-good host under change control.
troubleshoot-vdi-performance.symptom_match: "VDI session is not working", "Application is slow or unresponsive".

troubleshoot-vdi-usb-redirection.title: Troubleshoot VDI USB redirection
prechecks: Confirm the USB device works locally and identify its device class.
Check Citrix/VMware/AVD USB redirection policy, client/agent version and whether the device class is intentionally restricted.
Distinguish generic USB redirection from optimised smart-card, security-token, scanner or storage redirection and follow the appropriate security policy.
troubleshoot-vdi-usb-redirection.rollback: Capture the existing VDI redirection policy/client state. Restore the previous approved policy/client if a confirmed change causes regression; do not weaken device-control policy to make an unsupported USB device redirect.
troubleshoot-vdi-usb-redirection.symptom_match: "VDI session is not working", "USB device is not working".

troubleshoot-voicemail-access.title: Troubleshoot voicemail access
prechecks: Check the applicable voice/Teams/PBX service health and the user's voicemail entitlement/licensing.
Verify voicemail/call-routing policy, mailbox/voicemail provisioning and whether the issue is access, greeting, deposit or notification.
Use a controlled test message/call and review provider/admin diagnostics where available.
troubleshoot-voicemail-access.rollback: Capture the current voicemail/call policy before change. Restore the previous approved policy/provisioning state if an authorised change causes regression.

troubleshoot-windows-audio-output.title: Troubleshoot Windows audio output
prechecks: Check selected playback device, volume/mute and Windows audio service/device state.
Test audio in another application and with a known-good output device to separate application, driver and hardware scope.
Check Device Manager and recent driver/update changes.
troubleshoot-windows-audio-output.rollback: Record the current driver/device configuration. Restore the previous approved driver/configuration if a confirmed supported driver change caused regression.
troubleshoot-windows-audio-output.symptom_match: "Windows device is not working correctly", "Audio or microphone is not working".
troubleshoot-windows-audio-output.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

troubleshoot-wsl.title: Troubleshoot WSL
prechecks: Check `wsl --status`, installed distributions and Windows virtualization/WSL feature state.
Check disk space, WSL service/runtime errors and distribution health before reset/reinstall.
Export or otherwise preserve the affected distribution/data before unregistering or reinstalling it.
troubleshoot-wsl.rollback: Do not unregister/delete a distribution before an export/backup exists. If an approved WSL/runtime update causes regression, use the supported Windows/WSL recovery path or import the preserved distribution into a known-good runtime.

unlock-a-user-account.title: Unlock a user account
prechecks: This standard access-recovery page must route to the canonical user-account access-recovery procedure.
Verify identity before any unlock/password action and distinguish a one-time lockout from repeated lockouts, brute force or suspected compromise.
unlock-a-user-account.rollback: There is no meaningful 'undo' for an unlock. If the account immediately relocks, stop repeated unlocking and trace the lockout source. Suspected malicious lockout activity must route to Security Operations.
unlock-a-user-account.symptom_match: "Cannot sign in", "Access is denied or missing".
unlock-a-user-account.duplication: Related to Batch B-1 #9 (Password Reset) and B-1 #21 (Account Lockout). Merge these into a unified "User Account Access Recovery" procedure.

validate-a-backup-restore-request.title: Validate a backup restore request
prechecks: Step 0: verify the restore request, data owner/requester, approval, exact source data, requested restore point and retention/legal constraints before any restore.
Validate that the backup/restore point is catalogued and usable; perform an isolated test/verification where policy or criticality requires it.
Prefer an alternate restore destination or protected recovery location so current production data is not overwritten until the restored data is validated.
validate-a-backup-restore-request.rollback: A destructive overwrite may be irreversible. Preserve/snapshot the current destination where supported, stop immediately if the restore targets the wrong data/location, and restore/cut back to the preserved known-good state under the approved recovery plan.
validate-a-backup-restore-request.symptom_match: "Business data is missing, corrupted or requires recovery".

validate-accessories-issued-with-a-devic.title: Validate accessories issued with a device
prechecks: Check the authoritative asset record for expected accessories and ownership/custody.
Verify the physical accessories and identifiers where applicable, recording discrepancies without fabricating missing evidence.
Route missing/damaged accessories to the organisation's asset/loss process rather than treating inventory validation as an incident.
validate-accessories-issued-with-a-devic.rollback: Inventory validation itself has no technical rollback. Correct an erroneous asset-record update through the approved asset-management audit trail rather than deleting history.
validate-accessories-issued-with-a-devic.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

verify-data-after-a-migration.title: Verify data after a migration
prechecks: Compare source and destination object/file counts, aggregate sizes and migration-tool success/error reports.
Validate representative or risk-based samples using hashes/checksums where practical, plus open/read tests for critical file types.
Verify permissions/ownership, timestamps/metadata and application-specific integrity before final cutover.
verify-data-after-a-migration.rollback: If verification fails, halt/fail back the cutover and keep the source environment/data protected and authoritative until discrepancies are reconciled. Do not decommission or overwrite the source until acceptance criteria pass.
verify-data-after-a-migration.symptom_match: "Business data is missing, corrupted or requires recovery" (indirect).
